title: Protocol harmonization checklist for Responses -> OpenAI mapping
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: produce an operational checklist and executable mitigation plan that maps Redwood's Responses-compatible API surface to the OpenAI Responses protocol, focusing on areas that commonly cause lossiness: streaming semantics, tool/function calling handoff, structured output encoding, and metadata provenance. Deliverable is a checklist + test harness tasks + migration runbook for canary deploys.
acceptance_criteria: Clear mapping table of OpenAI Responses event types to Redwood runtime events (stream, delta, done, error)
Documented heuristics for detecting and handling partial/dropped function calls during streaming
Test harness with 25 canonical scenarios (stream termination, nested function call, structured JSON-LD payloads, tool error retry) defined as runnable test cases
Telemetry events and lossiness metrics defined with thresholds for automatic rollback (loss_score > 0.05 triggers canary pause)
Rollout plan that includes a staged traffic split, stepwise increase, and automated fallback to existing contract-preserving adapter
technical_design: We will implement a compatibility shim in the runtime proxy layer that performs three main transformations: 1) event normalization: convert OpenAI events (response.delta, response.done, response.error, response.tool_call) into Redwood internal stream events, preserving token provenance metadata; 2) function-call reconciliation: introduce an idempotent function-call ledger per session to deduplicate retries and detect in-flight tool acknowledgement mismatches; 3) structured-output canonicalizer: schema-aware parser that rewrites JSON/text structured output into Redwood's structured-output envelope and emits validation errors as structured events rather than plain text errors. The shim runs as a per-tenant plugin, configurable by routing policy.
migration_steps: Inventory existing endpoints that advertise Responses compatibility and tag by feature use (streaming-only, function-calling, structured-output, combined)
Create canonical scenario suite (see test_plan) and wire upstream mocks for OpenAI-style event sequences
Implement event normalization module with unit tests for edge cases (truncated chunk, reordered delta, mid-stream tool_call)
Add function-call ledger and reconciliation hooks into runtime session store (KV-backed with TTL)
Deploy shim behind feature flag for 5% of traffic in canary region eu-west-1
Monitor lossiness and functional correctness metrics for 72 hours, iterate on heuristics
Progressively increase traffic to 25% then 100% while exercising rollback on threshold breaches
test_plan: TP1: Streaming termination mismatch - client receives done event before kernel flush; assert token-completion parity
TP2: Delta reordering - out-of-order delta fragments arrive; assert reassembly correctness and token provenance stamps
TP3: Mid-stream function_call initiation - tool_call event appears interleaved with deltas; assert function args integrity and single invocation
TP4: Function retry dedup - duplicated tool_call idempotency under network retry; assert ledger prevents duplicate invocations
TP5: Structured-output partial JSON - stream produces partial JSON chunks that require reassembly and validation
TP6: Schema mismatch - structured output does not conform to expected JSON schema; assert shim emits structured validation event and does not silently drop payload
TP7: Tool error propagation - tool returns domain error; assert error surfaced with original token offsets and suggested client retry semantics
TP8: Cancellation race - client cancels while tool_call in-flight; assert correct cleanup of ledger and no orphaned tool executions
TP9: Token provenance audit - verify provenance headers are attached to each emitted token chunk
TP10: Backcompat regression - existing Redwood clients (non-OpenAI) behave unchanged under shim
telemetry: Emit these events: compat.shim.received_event, compat.shim.normalized_event, compat.shim.lossy_delta (with loss_score tag), compat.shim.toolcall_dedup, compat.shim.validation_error. Metrics: loss_score (float), percent_unhandled_toolcalls, avg_stream_latency_ms, function_call_dup_rate. Hook these into existing Alerts: loss_score > 0.05 for 30m OR function_call_dup_rate > 0.01 triggers P1 pager.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flagged deploy to staging with full test suite. Phase 1: Canary at 5% traffic in non-critical region with increased logging. Phase 2: 25% for 48h with automated checks. Phase 3: 100% with quiet-mode (reduced logging) and retention of detailed traces for 7 days. At each step evaluate ACs and metrics; automated rollback if any threshold breached. Post-rollout: monitor for 14 days and run regression harness nightly.
risks: Lossiness from semantic differences in tool_call vs function_call payload shapes
Client library assumptions about streaming event atomicity may break under normalized events
Increased latency from ledger lookups for function deduplication on high QPS sessions
Edge cases where structured output is intentionally non-JSON (e.g., mixed markdown + JSON) leading to false positives in validation
Incorrect rollback could leave client sessions pinned to incompatible model variants
